preparation.patch_format_normalization: Optional blank context prefixes removed; source content unchanged

certificate.accepted_domain: Nonnegative finite binary64 x and integer n3..8: subnormals round to zero; normal x=A*2^e with odd A is accepted when bit_length(A)*n<=64.
argument: A normal binary64 significand F is a nonzero 53-bit integer. F & (0-F) equals its lowest set bit 2^t, so 63-clz64 of that value is exactly t. Thus A=F>>t is odd and has width w=53-t.
If w*n<=64, every positive partial power A^i for 1<=i<=n is at most (2^w-1)^i<2^64. The finite table checks these monotone upper bounds for every eligible width and exponent.
For P=H*2^32+L, P*A=(H*A+floor(L*A/2^32))*2^32+(L*A mod2^32). The exact wide32 computes L*A; the high sum equals floor(P*A/2^32)<2^32, so the source split multiply loses no bit and cannot overflow.
Since n>=3, w<=21 and t>=32. Therefore a normal accepted input necessarily has its low32 encoding bits zero. The public gate omits no supported normal input.
After stripping t zeros, x^n=A^n*2^((field-1075+t)*n) exactly. All exponent calculations fit signed32bits, and the coefficient is nonzero with leading bit between0 and63.

Normalizing the exact integer coefficient to bit55 uses either an exact left shift or a right shift with a sticky low bit. No rounding occurs at this stage. Sticky shifts compose, including the further subnormal shift in the existing Binary<52,11>::pack.

The pack operation retains three guard/round/sticky bits and performs the single final round-to-nearest, ties-to-even step, then handles significand carry and overflow. This is exactly binary64 RNE of the original dyadic value, rather than rounded intermediate powers.
For 0<=x<2^-1022 and n>=3, x^n<2^-3066<2^-1075, so zero is the exact RNE result. The unchanged public negative-base integer path applies the exact sign after magnitude rounding.
limitations: These are source-pinned algebraic/range lemmas, not machine-checked verification of every compiled instruction.
The existing pack primitive and saved-register ABI are separately qualified by actual ARM integer-oracle and MPFR tests.
The helper does not extend the general pow totality guarantee beyond the existing exact stage; the general undecided trap is retained.

rounding.oracle: Directed MPFR bounds; both endpoints round to the same binary64 (RNE).
rounding.abi: Every call verifies R4-R11, SP, bounded stack writes.
rounding.semantics: RNE return values; errno and floating exception flags are not implemented.
rounding.nan_result_policy: NaN results must be quiet; payload and sign are unspecified.
known_limitations: An undecided owned 1024-bit pow refinement still traps; all-input totality is unproved.
rounding.scope: Finite corpus, not an exhaustive proof over every binary64 input.

argument: Normal x=A*2^e with odd A has w=bit_length(A). If w*n<=64, every partial positive integer power is below 2^64.
For n>=3, the accepted odd coefficient has at most 21bits; its factor fits uint32_t and the split multiplication computes the full exact uint64_t product.
Normalization followed by sticky shifts and the existing binary64 pack performs one final ties-to-even rounding, including subnormal and overflow boundaries.
A subnormal nonnegative x raised to any n>=3 is below the half-minimum-subnormal threshold and rounds to zero.
exact_short_ARM.scope: All normal exponent fields, coefficient width transitions, deterministic random short coefficients, exact midpoint examples, gradual underflow, overflow and public negative-base parity. Python computes the complete arbitrary-precision significand power and one final integer RNE rounding; no floating pow or libm oracle. Finite implementation qualification complements the exact algebraic bound.

changed_corpus_selection.predicate: Positive integer y3..8; finite magnitude x with low32bits zero; subnormal or odd-coefficient width*n<=64. Includes negative bases and may include inputs handled by earlier special cases.
changed_corpus_selection.scope: Complete source-line selection from the old million-case corpus for the newly accepted exact branch, not a new full-corpus run.

changed_corpus_qualification.oracle: Directed MPFR bounds must round to the same binary64; signaling NaNs separately require a quiet NaN result.
changed_corpus_qualification.abi: Every ARM call verifies R4-R11, SP and bounded stack writes.
changed_corpus_qualification.scope: Saved worst-case corpus; not a totality proof over all binary64 pairs.
known_limitations: The owned 512/1024-bit fallback preserves a final undecided-interval trap; totality is unproved.

ordinary_instruction_profile.scope: Executed ARM instructions on the prepared finite corpus, with typed 32-bit return masking. If sides_share_elf is false, owned production symbols and pinned diagnostic Qfplib symbols run on separate instances of the same Cortex-M0 emulator. When actual_bootrom is present, SDK ROM lookup initializers, wrappers and ROM bodies execute without intrinsic models. SIO division remains functionally modeled. These are not hardware cycles, cache comparisons, timings, or proof of speed parity.

hard_pow_before.scope: Seeded reservoir of published hard pow inputs in three explicit finite domains. Positive normal bases and bounded logarithm-products keep the composed Qfplib ln/mul/exp comparison meaningful. Actual production/diagnostic ARM and captured ROM execute on separate identical emulator instances. Instruction counts are not physical cycles or timings. This is additional coverage, not a replacement for the 114-group matrix or an all-input proof.

cache_models.assumptions: Same previously checked 16 KiB / two-way / 8-byte-line cache geometry; LRU/FIFO replacement and whole-line/per-word fills are explicit model assumptions. These are not claims about undocumented prefetch or replacement.
cache_models.scope: Exact ARM instruction/data traces and exact results on nine finite groups per image, with actual ROM and linked memory code. Two warm passes then a measured third pass. Only XIP accesses enter the cache model. Excludes caller prefetch, IRQs, other-core traffic and Qfplib batches. Not measured XIP counters or physical speed evidence.

M4.scope: Cortex-M4 O3 release, both soft and hard float ABIs: normalized preprocessing and every allocated code/data section identical; existing M4 runtime sources byte-identical

generic_M0.scope: Non-RP2040 generic ARMv6-M: every allocated code/data section remains byte-identical to V60. The generic spelling has an extra expression macro; normalized preprocessing identity is not claimed.

counter_regression.scope: Actual ROM/flash/SRAM code; mixed counted and uncounted calls must have the same nonzero instruction count as a fresh machine. This guards emulator instrumentation, not hardware timing.

scope: Qualified private RP2040 prototype on the unaccepted platform and flash-memory candidate. Full million-case numerical qualification belongs to V79; V81 separately checks the complete 5717-entry new-acceptance subset, 27647 exact-integer cases, public callers and 265409 MPFR cases. No all-input totality or physical speed claim.
remains: Eliminate the three observed hard pow instruction-count gaps and add these streams to the physical comparison; the previous 114 groups are insufficient for the complete speed audit.
General pow totality outside the exact stage 224 exponents remains unproved; its undecided trap is retained.
